Absolute node counts and spherical placements are provisional deterministic hypotheses rather than unique scientific reconstructions.
Ancient and non-Earth tectonic regimes may preserve structural families that are not represented by the current seven-family vocabulary.
Continental-kernel records are deep structural identity hypotheses and do not assert exposed land, coastlines, elevation, or habitability.
Ice-shell and mixed-composition bodies lack a dedicated non-rocky spatial-structure vocabulary and therefore remain especially uncertain.
No geologic-spine output may write terrain, land-water classification, sea level, climate, hydrology, biomes, materials, resources, or rendering state.
Plume, rift, convergence, transform, accretion, basin, and kernel associations do not imply a unique plate reconstruction.
W1-05 does not rasterize boundaries or create final plate polygons; it records resolution-independent spherical identities and ancestry only.
